dayLines: You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
🪤 A person, maybe 40s, with freckles is back. "Snares were empty. They'll keep."
Recipe: Snare (Level 1). You have seen a snare. A loop, a stick, an animal.

🪤 A person, maybe 40s, with freckles catches you watching the snares come off the line. "...Want to actually SEE one?" They show you — the loop, the trigger stick, where the run narrows between the roots. "Opossum trails. Check at dawn. Always." Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
💧 A person, maybe 30s returns with water: +2 clean.
💧 A woman, maybe 30s, with weathered hands returns with water: +3 clean.
"Hey." A woman, maybe 20s settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A woman, maybe 20s.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A woman, maybe 20s is humming something. It stops when they notice you listening.
A woman, maybe 30s, with ink-stained fingers traded something with someone for something else. The barter economy stirs.
Ruth and Tyrone lingered over the fire together.
Nina and Tyrone lingered over the fire together.
You remember the Sharpened stick at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
You remember the Good Boots at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.

Travel 1 tile to meadow.
— Open ground —
Grasshoppers rise in a clicking wave ahead of you. Something fork-tailed rides the wind above them, waiting for the careless ones.
Something big is moving in the woods. The birds went quiet.
Movement — a fat groundhog, whistling an alarm from its haunches.
👁 It whistles when it clocks you — and the whole meadow hears it. Wind it before it reaches the burrow, or hunt the whistlers last.
You catch fragments by the fire — Hattie telling A man, maybe 60s, with a shaved head about you. The details have shifted. Nobody seems to mind.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Travel 2 tiles to grove.
— Nut trees —
A hollow log big enough to crawl into. You don't crawl in. You note where it is, in case the weather ever makes the offer again.
Something moves out there — two knobs on glass-still water, watching.
Movement — a gray squirrel, chattering.
👁 It'll go straight up a tree when spooked. Bring something ranged, or wait it out.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Travel 2 tiles to trail edge.
— An old trail —
The trail is worn smooth as an old coin. Deer, probably. Probably.
You see smoke on the horizon. Stonebridge — 12 people, 3 days in. fishing folk, by the look of it. They know 2 plants — 2 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
Unfamiliar unknown berries — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
Journal: Trampled ground. The humble weeds win.

A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 4× unknown berries. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.

🛟 Tyrone stands up by the fire. "The sick can't wait us out. Somebody has to say it, so: we need a plan, tonight. Here's what we CAN do — pick one, maybe two, but everything costs something."
"Triage tents and broth for the sick, or half rations till it passes, or the healthy hunt hard to keep everyone fed. Pick — everything costs."
"Or we rally," Tyrone adds. "Second shift, everybody. We work, we eat, we live — and we pay for it."
(Relief is open — triage, rations, hunt, or rally, from the beats row. Each option works once; the moment passes in ~3 days.)
